llm.summary: This is a coherent VMware audit and policy helper, but it needs Review because it records broad operational audit data and its policy protections can fail open or be globally bypassed.

dimensions.detail: The local audit database records parameters, results, agent, workflow, user, status, and risk level for many VMware tools; this is expected for audit logging but may capture sensitive infrastructure data and exports are lightly warned.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation is via a uv package and Bash-enabled CLI use; the artifacts do not show hidden install steps, background services, or network callbacks, but this depends on an external package not included in the artifact.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Activation across all VMware skill tool calls is disclosed and mostly purpose-aligned, but the documented global policy bypass and fail-open states are broad for a component positioned as mandatory security infrastructure.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Persistent local audit storage and hot-reloaded policy config are disclosed, but enforcement allows all operations when rules are missing, can be disabled with VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED=1, and reportedly allows all operations if PyYAML is absent.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose, audit logging, policy checks, sanitization, and decorator behavior fit together as shared infrastructure for VMware skills; it does not expose its own MCP tools or claim unrelated capabilities.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with local audit logs containing VMware operational details, protect ~/.vmware/audit.db and exported files, configure ~/.vmware/rules.yaml before relying on enforcement, and avoid setting VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED=1 outside a controlled break-glass situation.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] expected: The auto-loaded dependency model is disclosed in SKILL.md and fits a shared decorator-based policy/audit library, so this alone is not a material concern.
[SQP-2] expected: Recording parameters and results to ~/.vmware/audit.db is central to the audit purpose, but the artifact shows broad fields that may include sensitive VMware operational data unless callers correctly mark sensitive parameters.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The artifact-backed VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED=1 bypass disables all policy checks while allowing operations to proceed, which is a material concern for a policy layer spanning high-impact VMware tools.
[SQP-2] expected: Exporting audit logs is expected for compliance workflows, but the examples encourage stdout/file export without strong handling guidance for potentially sensitive audit records.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The setup guide documents the same global bypass without clearly limiting it to break-glass or development use.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The setup guide states that missing ~/.vmware/rules.yaml allows all operations, which creates a fail-open default for users expecting active policy enforcement after installation.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The troubleshooting guide states that missing PyYAML silently allows all operations, a weak failure mode for security infrastructure.
